title: AI-Powered Personalized Financial Planning Systems: A Systematic Review and Future Research Directions
authors: Balog, A.; Nechita, E.; Mihai, S.
venue: Open Journal of Psychology and Social Sciences
tldr: A systematic review of 45 studies reveals key design principles for AI-powered personalized financial planning systems including adaptability, transparency, and user-centricity.
problem_and_motivation: The proliferation of AI technologies has created opportunities for personalized financial planning systems, but the field lacks a comprehensive understanding of design principles, architectural patterns, and effectiveness metrics. Existing reviews focus on specific applications rather than providing a holistic view of system design requirements.
approach: Conducted a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines.
Analyzed 45 peer-reviewed studies from 2018 to 2024 on AI-powered financial planning systems.
Categorized systems by architecture type: rule-based, ML-based, hybrid, and LLM-based.
Extracted design principles, effectiveness metrics, and implementation challenges.
Synthesized findings into a framework for system design and evaluation.
Identified gaps in current research and proposed future research directions.
findings: num: 45 studies analyzed in the systematic review.
num: 73% of systems used hybrid architectures combining multiple AI techniques.
num: 89% incorporated some form of personalization.
num: 67% addressed explainability as a key design requirement.
num: 78% reported user satisfaction scores above 75%.
The most effective systems combined rule-based logic with ML-based personalization.

definitions.definition: Financial planning systems that adapt recommendations based on individual user characteristics, goals, and behaviors.
System design that combines multiple AI techniques such as rule-based logic, ML, and NLP to leverage their respective strengths.
The degree to which a system can provide clear, understandable explanations for its recommendations and decisions.
The incorporation of insights from behavioral finance research into system design to account for cognitive biases and emotional factors.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic review provides a comprehensive framework for designing and evaluating AI-powered personalized financial planning systems. It identifies that hybrid architectures combining rule-based logic with ML personalization are most effective, and establishes key design principles including adaptability, transparency, and user-centricity. The review synthesizes 45 studies to create actionable guidelines for system designers.
directly_justifies: Hybrid AI architectures combining rule-based and ML approaches are most effective for financial planning systems.
User personalization and explainability are critical design requirements for adoption and trust.
Behavioral finance insights should be integrated into system design to improve outcomes.
limits: Review limited to peer-reviewed studies; may miss industry implementations.
Rapid AI development may quickly outdated specific technical findings.
English-language bias in the systematic review process.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 2 (User Perspectives) applies through 2.A (User Needs and Preferences). Domain 4 (Existing Systems) applies through 4.A (Current Tools). Domain 7 (Budgeting Strategies) is highly relevant through 7.A (Rule-Based and AI-Driven Systems) and 7.B (AI and LLM-Based Analysis). Domain 12 (Evaluation Frameworks) is highly relevant through 12.A (System Evaluation) and 12.D (Benchmarking). Other domains like 1, 3, 5-6, 8-11, 13-14 are less directly applicable.

limitations: Peer-reviewed study bias may exclude valuable industry implementations.
Review timeframe (2018-2024) may miss earlier foundational work or the most recent developments.
English-language limitation may exclude relevant non-English studies.
Synthesized findings represent average effectiveness; individual system performance varies.
remember_this: 73% of effective systems used hybrid architectures combining multiple AI techniques.
67% addressed explainability as a key design requirement.
Hybrid rule-based + ML personalization is the most effective architecture pattern.
